title: Identifying Linear-Gaussian DAGs from Gaussian Copulas under Known Innovation Multipliers
banked_reason: The note proves the advertised sharp generic identification frontier only within an acyclic linear-Gaussian model having exactly known, coordinatewise normalized innovation multipliers and fixed vertex correspondence; complete-DAG-only cubic recovery, factorial sparse traversal, fixed-p strong-margin inference, and no applied demonstration cap the sound result at subfield.
gap_reasons: The claimed cubic recovery result is confined to generic complete DAGs, while arbitrary sparse fibers still require factorial order traversal and the output-sensitive enumeration question remains open.

The confidence set has finite-sample coverage, but informative singleton recovery requires imposed conditioning, beta-min, wrong-order separation, exact calibration, and fixed p, with no numerical study showing that these thresholds yield useful sets at realistic sample sizes.

Those scope restrictions, the unresolved sparse computation problem, and the absence of an applied or simulation demonstration constrain the leading-journal score despite the delivered field-level identification theorem.
proof_attempt_summary: The derivation established the sound sharp generic projective-schedule frontier, tied-profile counterexamples, canonical recovery, a cubic complete-DAG procedure, and fixed-p rank-summary confidence sets; both D0.5 mathematical panels passed with no findings. The field-tier package collapsed at the contribution gate because general sparse recovery remained factorial and practical singleton recovery depended on strong margins without an empirical demonstration. A future re-raise should supply genuinely output-sensitive or polynomial-delay sparse enumeration, or comparably substantial new robustness and applied architecture, rather than repeat the completed perturbation analysis.
tldr: Known reference-normalized innovation multipliers can identify an invariant linear-Gaussian DAG even when every site releases only a Gaussian copula. The true structural coefficients are represented by the unit-free canonical matrix \(B^0=B^{\pi_0}(R_0)=H_0BH_0^{-1}\). Pairwise projective separation is the sharp universal generic frontier: wrong orders fail polynomial prediction identities, whereas tied profiles admit explicit reverse-edge and fork--chain twins. Exact all-order recovery uses signed squared-cross-product checks inside its construction, while the substantive conditional-pair theorem proves complete-DAG generic completeness and \(O(Ep^3)\) complexity. Uniform predictor bounds turn Kendall summaries into honest graph confidence sets under an explicit bounded normalized-excitation design regularity; the beta-min threshold, separation margin, and fallback are all expressed in reference-standardized units. Exact-once sparse-fiber enumeration remains open.
gap: Montagna2025InvariancePrinciple, Section 3, Theorem 1, is the closest multiple-environment identifiability comparator, but it uses full environment densities through score and Hessian information and needs two auxiliary environments. BACKSHIFT uses covariance differences on a common numerical scale. GnIES arXiv:2211.14897v4, Theorem 6, uses full Gaussian environment distributions; the separate Journal of Machine Learning Research article by Taeb, Gamella, Heinze-Deml, and Bühlmann treats latent variables and unknown additive interventions. Invariant prediction tests stability of a response conditional law across environments, and conditional-variance identification uses scale-bearing observational quantities. None characterizes the full DAG fiber or honest support uncertainty from independently standardized correlations and a known normalized excitation schedule, including the reference-plus-one-environment frontier.
fill: The project proves the universal generic if-and-only-if frontier and tied-profile necessity family, uses the reference-standardized coordinate \(B^0=H_0BH_0^{-1}\), gives a non-tautological conditional-pair completeness and cubic-complexity theorem for generic complete DAGs, and closes rank-summary inference under explicit gauge-invariant margins and bounded calibrated design profiles. Signed polynomial checks remain part of the exhaustive algorithm specification, not a separate contribution.
